package.title: Reliable saving, atomic compute commit and mosaic integrity
package.goal: No edit, rename or laid stone is lost on reload or tab close, and no failed save goes unnoticed. A compute that finishes in the background never corrupts the saved project and never brings a deleted project back. The saved record and the mosaic always belong together. The hook also provides the backup and manual-edit API that the wave-2 recompute guard needs.
steps: db.ts tx(): after the single request of a readwrite transaction, call t.commit() if it exists. Reset the cached dbp on db.onclose and db.onversionchange. If transaction() throws InvalidStateError, retry once with a new connection. Add a txMulti(stores, mode, fn) helper. Make deleteProject one transaction over all four stores.

db.ts: add optional fields to ProjectRecord: mosaicRev, imageRev, computedImageRev, meta.manualEdits. Add saveMosaicAndProgress(id, mosaic, progress), which writes both in one transaction over mosaics+progress. Add commitComputed(id, fields, mosaicWithRev, progress) as one readwrite transaction over projects, mosaics and progress. Inside request callbacks only (no other awaits), it reads the LATEST stored record. If the record is missing, abort and reject with Error('deleted'). Otherwise merge only the compute-owned fields (palette, diagnostics, computedWith, mosaicRev, computedImageRev, meta.computed/thumb/updatedAt, meta.manualEdits=0), then put the record, the mosaic and the progress.
serialize.ts: add an optional rev to StoredMosaic and keep it through pack/unpack.

src/core/integrity.ts: add maxColorIndex(data). It scans c1, plus c2 only for DIAG/LINE kinds, plus every sub array and free[].color. Add checkMosaicIntegrity(rec, stored) returning {ok, reason:'rev'|'index'|null}. Legacy data with no rev on either side passes the rev check.

useProject saving: change saveTimers to entries of {t, fn}. schedule() stores fn. flush() runs every pending fn plus every key in a failedKeys set via Promise.allSettled. The 'mosaic' job calls saveMosaicAndProgress, so progress is always saved together with the mosaic. Call flush on beforeunload, pagehide, and visibilitychange when hidden, each as flush().catch(()=>{}). Debounces become: rec 250 ms, progress 150 ms, mosaic 300 ms.

Save state: expose saveState ('saved'|'saving'|'error'), saveError {code:'quota'|'connection'|'other', message}, retrySave() (= flush), and exportCurrent(). exportCurrent returns a Blob built from IN-MEMORY rec, image and packMosaic(computed.data) through a new projects.ts buildProjectExport(rec, image, mosaic, progress). Refactor exportProject to use the same function. When a save fails, keep its key dirty and retry with backoff (2 s, 5 s, 15 s, 60 s).

compute(): use the snapshot r only to build the worker inputs. After the worker returns, set computedWith = computeKey(snapshot), or for custom mode computeKey of the snapshot with res.palette. Also set mosaicRev = uid() and computedImageRev = r.imageRev. Call await commitComputed(...). If it rejects with 'deleted', set computeError('deleted') and stop. On success, merge with setRec(prev => ({...prev, ...computeFields, meta:{...prev.meta,...}})); never spread the snapshot. Clear pending rec/mosaic/progress timers that belong to the replaced grid.

Loader: use a stored mosaic only when checkMosaicIntegrity passes. If it fails, set computed=null and expose integrityError = 'mismatch' so the UI can ask for a recompute. Never render a palette and grid that do not belong together.
Image identity: setPhoto sets imageRev = uid(). computeKey adds `im: r.imageRev` and omits it when undefined, so keys of legacy projects stay byte-identical.

Manual edits and backup: touchMosaic increments rec.meta.manualEdits. Expose manualEdits. Expose createBackupCopy(suffix): await flush(), then duplicateProject(id, suffix), returning the new id. duplicateProject copies the rev fields.
Bitmaps: release a replaced or unmounted ImageBitmap through a useEffect cleanup keyed on the bitmap. In the load effect, call bmp.close() when !alive.
acceptance: typecheck, test and build are green. tests/w1-persistence.test.ts covers maxColorIndex for all CellKinds, checkMosaicIntegrity for the rev and index cases, and checks that computeKey(rec without imageRev) equals the pre-change key string while setting imageRev changes it.
e2e reload: recolour J020, toggle 5 stones in lay mode and rename, then reload after 50 ms. All three changes persist.
e2e: rename and change the joint while a compute is running (city sample, 4 mm tiles). After the compute the name is still in IndexedDB and api.stale is true (stale badge visible).
e2e: leave during a compute, reopen, rename, reload. The stored palette.length equals maxColorIndex+1, and record.mosaicRev equals mosaic.rev.
e2e: delete the project during a compute. It does not reappear after the compute finishes and the page reloads.
e2e: change a laid stone's shape and navigate away immediately. After reopening, the stone's laid checkbox is unchecked.
e2e: patch IDBObjectStore.put to throw QuotaExceededError. No unhandled rejection occurs. After unpatching, the next edit plus a reload persists the earlier rename, because dirty keys are retried.
package.risk: Effort L. This package changes the core save path. Keep the schema backward compatible: legacy records without rev must still load, so the index check is the only guard for them. Run the existing e2e flow before merging.

findings.title: Leaving a project while it is still computing, then reopening it, corrupts the saved project: the mosaic is rendered and printed with the wrong palette
findings.problem: compute() runs in a module-level worker channel and keeps running after the Workspace unmounts. When it finishes, it saves its own record and mosaic. If the user reopens the project in the meantime, the new useProject instance loads the OLD record and mosaic. It shows no 'computing' indicator. Its next save of the record (any rename or setting change) overwrites the record written by compute but leaves compute's new mosaic in place. Record and mosaic are saved by unrelated, non-atomic puts. Nothing ties them together (no revision), so the loader accepts any pair that has the same cols×rows. As a result, colour indices from one compute are mapped onto the palette of another. The same race applies to two open browser tabs.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t10_leave_during_compute.cjs, output in t10_output.txt in the same folder. City sample, 260,241 positions. Compute with 16 colours, then switch to 8 colours and recompute. Leave via 'Meine Projekte', reopen ('palette rows = 16, computing indicator visible: false'), rename, reload. Result: 'palette rows = 16', and the legend shows 01..08 used and 09..16 with 0 stones. The city is rendered in pink/yellow; screenshot t10-after-reload.png in the same folder. Code: useProject.ts:331-346 (compute saves rec, mosaic and progress with Promise.all as 3 separate transactions, from the snapshot r); useProject.ts:86-94 (loader only checks layout.cols/rows); client.ts:5-12 (one global 'compute' worker, with no per-project job state); db.ts:96-102 (independent puts).
findings.proposal: (1) Track jobs per project in a small module-level registry, e.g. src/workers/jobs.ts with Map<projectId, {promise, progress}>. useProject subscribes on mount, so a reopened Workspace shows the running compute and its Cancel button and refreshes when the job finishes. (2) Add db.saveComputed(id, rec, mosaic, progress), which writes all three stores in ONE IndexedDB transaction (db.transaction(['projects','mosaics','progress'],'readwrite')). (3) Add a revision: rec.mosaicRev = uid() is written together with mosaic.rev. The loader shows the mosaic only if rec.mosaicRev === mosaic.rev && max colour index < palette.length. Otherwise it shows 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen' instead of rendering wrong colours. (4) Optimistic concurrency in saveProject: inside one readwrite transaction, read the stored meta.rev, refuse to overwrite a newer revision, and tell the user (this also covers two tabs).
corrected:
(1) Move compute ownership out of the component. Create src/workers/jobs.ts with Map<projectId, {promise, progress, cancel}>.
- The job itself does the final persist, so it no longer depends on setRec/setComputed of a possibly unmounted hook.
- useProject subscribes on mount. A reopened Workspace then shows the running progress and the Cancel button, and adopts the result (setRec + setComputed) when the job resolves.

(2) Add saveComputed(id, computedFields, mosaic, progress) in src/storage/db.ts. It runs ONE readwrite transaction over ['projects','mosaics','progress']:
- Read the CURRENT stored record.
- Merge in only the compute-owned fields: palette, diagnostics, computedWith, meta.computed, meta.thumb, and a new mosaicRev = uid().
- Put the record, the mosaic {...mosaic, rev: mosaicRev} and the progress in that same transaction.
This way a rename or other edit made during the compute is not lost, and record and mosaic can never be half-written.

(3) Make the loader in useProject.ts:85-98 validate the pair. Accept the stored mosaic only if rec.mosaicRev === mosaic.rev AND every colour index (c1, c2, subCol, free[].color) is less than palette.length. Otherwise do not render it. Show a clear notice such as 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen' and keep the Preview, Plan and PDF steps disabled until the user recomputes.
- The palette-length check alone is not enough. In the photo-replace and two-tab repros the indices are within range and the stale badge is not shown.
- Treat legacy records without a rev the same way: run the index-range check and show a soft warning.

(4) For saves from other instances (useProject.update and flush, and the two-tab case), change saveProject to run as one readwrite transaction:
- Read the stored record.
- If stored.mosaicRev differs from the in-memory rec.mosaicRev, keep the stored compute-owned fields (palette, computedWith, diagnostics, mosaicRev, thumb) and apply only the user's edits on top. Do not silently refuse the save.
- Post a BroadcastChannel('mosaicplan') message {id, mosaicRev} from saveComputed. Open tabs or instances of the same project then reload the record and mosaic, or show 'In einem anderen Tab neu berechnet – neu laden'.
- Palette edits made after the compute (custom names, material assignment) must update mosaicRev only when the mapping from colour index to colour changes. Edits that only change names keep the rev.

(5) Add an e2e test based on verify-correctness-ui-state-0/v1_leave_during_compute.cjs and v3_two_tabs.cjs. It must assert that after the reload the stored palette, the computedWith key and the mosaic all come from the same compute.

Fix in four parts, in this order of priority.

1) Commit compute results atomically and safely (src/storage/db.ts).
- Add commitComputed(id, patch, mosaic, progress, rev). It opens ONE transaction: db.transaction(['projects','mosaics','progress'], 'readwrite').
- Inside onsuccess callbacks only (no await on non-IDB promises), it does: get('projects', id).
  - If the record is missing (project was deleted), abort and reject with 'deleted'.
  - Otherwise put {...latest, palette, diagnostics, computedWith, mosaicRev: rev, meta: {...latest.meta, computed: true, thumb, updatedAt}}.
  - Then put mosaics[id] = {...packed, rev} and progress[id].
- Prepare thumb, packMosaic and computeKey BEFORE opening the transaction.
- computedWith = computeKey of the snapshot settings that were computed (in custom mode, together with the result palette), never of the merged record. This way, edits made during the compute correctly show as 'stale' and are not lost (this also fixes t2: rename and joint change during a compute).
- Also add a multi-store tx helper. deleteProject should use one transaction over all four stores.

2) Per-project job registry (new src/workers/jobs.ts).
- Holds Map<projectId, {progress, promise, cancel}> plus a subscribe(id, cb) API.
- Move the worker call and commitComputed out of the component closure into startCompute(id, input).
- Allow only one compute at a time across the app. If a job for another project is running, the compute button shows 'Berechnung für „<Name>“ läuft noch' with Abbrechen.
- useProject subscribes on mount:
  - It shows the running job's phase/fraction and the Cancel button.
  - On commit it does setRec(prev => ({...prev, palette, diagnostics, computedWith, mosaicRev, meta: {...prev.meta, computed: true, thumb}})).
  - It replaces computedRef/state with the committed grid.
  - It clears pending 'mosaic'/'progress' save timers that refer to the old grid.
- While a job is running for the project, disable stone edits on the old grid in a reopened instance.
- Projects.tsx: deleting a project with a running job cancels that job first.

3) Integrity guard in the loader (useProject.ts:85-98).
- Render the stored grid only if both conditions hold:
  - (rec.mosaicRev === undefined && mosaic.rev === undefined) [legacy data], OR rec.mosaicRev === mosaic.rev;
  - AND max colour index < rec.palette.length (a single pass over the Uint16 colour array).
- Otherwise, set computed = null. Show a banner (de/en/tr): 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen', with the Berechnen button. Never render, plan or print the mismatched pair.
- Every writer that changes what colour indices mean must write both revs in one transaction: compute, palette compaction/removal, and import. Manual stone edits that only append palette entries keep the existing rev, so they cannot trigger false positives.
- Include rev in export/duplicate. Imports without a rev take the legacy path.
- Also block the PDF and plan steps when stale is true, or at least show a prominent warning on the PDF cover/first page.

4) Instead of optimistic concurrency in saveProject, guard against two tabs with the Web Locks API.
- Workspace calls navigator.locks.request('project:' + id, {ifAvailable: true}, lock => lock ? new Promise(release on unmount) : null).
- If the lock is not granted, open the project read-only with the banner 'Dieses Projekt ist in einem anderen Tab geöffnet'.
- This avoids the false-conflict and silent-save-refusal risk of rev checks on every debounced save.

Tests:
- Extend e2e/run-e2e.cjs with these flows:
  - Leave during compute, reopen, check that progress and Cancel are visible, then rename, reload, and check palette length == max index + 1 and colours as computed.
  - The same, but set the colour count back, and check that no wrong grid is shown as 'berechnet'.
  - Delete during compute, then check that the project does not come back.
- Add a vitest unit test: the loader guard rejects a mismatched rev or an out-of-range index.

findings.title: Edits from the last 0.4–1.2 s are lost on reload or tab close because the 'pagehide' save never completes
findings.problem: Saves are debounced: the record after 400 ms, progress after 600 ms, the mosaic after 1200 ms. The only safety net is flush() on 'pagehide'/'visibilitychange'. flush() goes through open().then(...) and starts asynchronous IndexedDB transactions that the browser tears down before they commit. So stone colour or shape changes, lay-mode taps and renames made shortly before a reload or tab close are lost silently. On Android, switching apps fires 'visibilitychange' first, which mitigates this. On PC and tablet browsers (refresh, closing the tab, browser restart) the data is lost.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t4_reload_mid_edit.cjs. With a 50 ms delay (t4_output_50ms.txt): '(a) J020 colour 09 -> 13 ... after reload = 09 -> LOST', '(b) placed in UI = 5 ... after reload placed = 0', '(c) name ... = Test: Tier (Katze)'. At 500 ms the stone edit is still lost. At 1600 ms everything persists (t4_output_1600ms.txt). Trace t4b_pagehide_trace.cjs / t4b_output.txt: '[trace] pagehide at 3186', '[trace] put projects at 3187', then neither 'complete' nor 'abort' is logged. The write is issued but never committed. Code: useProject.ts:107-113 (schedule), 133-142 (pagehide flush), 151/166/179 (400/1200/600 ms).
findings.proposal: (1) Write progress and single-stone edits through almost immediately: coalesce with queueMicrotask or setTimeout(…,50) instead of 600/1200 ms. Saving progress is one Uint16Array put. For very large mosaics, store dirty cell indices in a small 'patches' store and compact later. (2) Keep the resolved IDBDatabase in a plain variable, so flush() can create its transaction synchronously inside the event handler. (3) On the web build, add a 'beforeunload' handler that calls e.preventDefault() while saveTimers is non-empty or a save is in flight, so the browser shows 'Seite verlassen?'. (4) Show a small 'Gespeichert ✓ / Speichert…' indicator in the Workspace header, driven by the same pending-save counter.
corrected:
1. In src/storage/db.ts tx(): after `const r = fn(s);`, add `if (mode === 'readwrite' && typeof (t as any).commit === 'function') (t as any).commit();`. Every write here issues exactly one request, so this is safe. It tells the browser to commit right away instead of waiting for the success callback, which never comes while the page is unloading.

2. In src/ui/project/useProject.ts, in the effect at lines 133-142, also register `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', h)` and remove it in the cleanup. 'beforeunload' fires before the old document is torn down, and together with commit() the write survives a reload (measured 5 of 5; the full app simulation persisted all edits).
   - Keep the existing 'pagehide' and 'visibilitychange' handlers, which cover Android app switching.
   - Do not save the whole mosaic every 50 ms.
   - Optionally lower the progress debounce from 600 ms to about 250 ms, since saving progress is a single Uint16Array put.

3. Optional fallback for very large mosaics, where packMosaic in flush() may be slow: in the same 'beforeunload' handler, call `e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''` only while Object.keys(saveTimers.current).length > 0 after flush has been started. This adds the browser's leave-page prompt on the web build only; it has no effect in the Capacitor app.

4. Optional: expose a pendingSaves counter, incremented in schedule() and decremented when each save promise settles. Show 'Speichert… / Gespeichert ✓' next to the title in the Workspace header (Workspace.tsx:52). Make the indicator turn red when a save promise rejects; today schedule() only calls console.error.

5. Add an e2e check: rename a project and change one stone's colour, reload after 50 ms, and assert both changes are still there.

(1) useProject.ts:133-142: also register the existing handler on window 'beforeunload' (no preventDefault) and keep 'pagehide'. Run the visibilitychange handler only when document.visibilityState === 'hidden'. Measured: with this alone the real app keeps the stone colour, 5 lay-mode taps and the rename at 0 ms and 50 ms reload delay.

(2) Fix flush() (115-131) so it matches the scheduled saves. If 'mosaic' or 'progress' is pending, save the packed mosaic AND saveProgress(id, c.data.progress), and save progress only once. This fixes the stale placed-bit seen in the auditor's t8.

(3) Shorten the debounces: progress 600 -> 100 ms, mosaic 1200 -> 200 ms, record 400 -> 250 ms. Measured: one full put of a 3M-cell mosaic costs about 18 ms on the main thread, so no patch store is needed. Drop the original idea of keeping the IDBDatabase in a plain variable: on its own it does not help, since synchronous transactions started in pagehide are still lost.

(4) Expose saveState ('saved' | 'saving' | 'error') from useProject:
- Count pending and in-flight saves.
- At line 111, set 'error' instead of only calling console.error.
- Show 'Gespeichert ✓ / Speichert … / Speichern fehlgeschlagen' in the Workspace header, with i18n keys in de/en/tr.
- Optionally, call preventDefault in beforeunload only while saveState === 'error'.

(5) Add an e2e regression test to e2e/run-e2e.cjs:
- Recolour J020, tap 5 stones in lay mode and rename the project.
- Reload after 50 ms.
- Assert that all three persisted.
- Also assert that changing a stone's shape and immediately leaving does not bring back old placed bits.

findings.title: Edits made while a compute is running are silently reverted, and the app then jumps to the Preview step
findings.problem: compute() takes r = recRef.current at the start and finishes with setRec({...r, palette, diagnostics, computedWith, meta}). Everything the user changed while the worker ran is overwritten in state and in IndexedDB: project name, joint, size, adjustments, regions, PDF options. Because computedWith is then the key of the old snapshot, the change does not even show as stale. The stepper and all inputs stay active during compute. When compute finishes, onDone() also forces the Preview step, even if the user is working in another step.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t2_edit_during_compute.cjs, output t2_output.txt: 'stillComputingWhenEdited: true, nameDuring: Umbenannt waehrend Berechnung, jointDuring: 3', then 'compute took ~ 838 ms; app jumped to step: 8Vorschau', '{ nameAfter: Test: Stadtbild, jointAfter: 2 }', and after reload the name is still 'Test: Stadtbild'. findings.proposal: In compute(), merge into the latest state instead of the snapshot: setRec(prev => ({...prev, palette: res.palette, diagnostics, computedWith: keyOfSnapshot, meta: {...prev.meta, computed: true, thumb}})). Keep computedWith = computeKey(snapshot), so edits made during the compute correctly show as stale. Save the merged object. Call onDone() only if the user is still on the compute step (keep a stepRef in Workspace), otherwise show a toast 'Berechnung fertig – Vorschau öffnen'. Optionally disable geometry and colour inputs while api.computing is set, with a note.

2) Stop palette edits that cannot be merged: in StepColors.tsx, wrap the palette table and the add/remove controls in <fieldset disabled={!!api.computing}>. Add a note (de/en/tr) such as 'Berechnung läuft – Farbänderungen sind danach wieder möglich'. Optionally do the same for stone editing in StoneDialog (color-pick), because recompute replaces that data anyway.

3) No forced jump: in Workspace.tsx add const stepRef = useRef(step); stepRef.current = step; and const [doneNotice, setDoneNotice] = useState(false). When doneNotice is set, show a badge button in ws-head next to the stale badge: 'Berechnung fertig – Vorschau öffnen' (i18n de/en/tr). Clicking it opens the preview step and clears the notice; also clear it when the user opens preview another way. The app has no toast component; this reuses the existing badge-as-button pattern from line 55.

4) While api.computing is set, show a small line in ws-head: 'Berechnung läuft (Phase, %) – Änderungen an Größe, Fuge, Fliesen, Farben und Formen gelten erst nach erneuter Berechnung'. Do not disable all geometry inputs: the merge plus the stale badge already keeps the state correct.

Then assert: the name and the joint are kept after compute and after a reload; the stale badge is visible (the joint is part of the compute key); the active step is still 'joint'; the done badge is visible; the drawn mosaic, legend and stats still use the computed 2 mm joint until the user recomputes.

findings.title: Replacing the photo after a compute is not detected as a change, so the PDF shows the new photo next to the old mosaic
findings.problem: computeKey contains layout, shapes, palette settings, adjust and regions, but nothing that identifies the image. setPhoto only resets crop, rotation and flip. If those were already at their defaults, the key is unchanged, so no stale badge appears anywhere. The old mosaic stays and is presented as current. The PDF takes its 'Originalfoto' from the CURRENT bitmap (api.originalPreview), so the plan pairs a city photo with a portrait mosaic. Face and detail regions from the old photo are also kept for the new one. The PDF step has no stale warning at all, even for normal setting changes.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t3_photo_replace_not_stale.cjs, output t3_output.txt: 'stale badge after replacing photo with city.png: false', 'preview stale badge: false'. The generated PDF t3-plan.pdf has the city skyline on page 2 'Originalfoto' and the portrait mosaic on pages 3-4; render: t3-pages-1-4.png in the same folder. Code: useProject.ts:18-32 (computeKey), 186-202 (setPhoto), StepPdf.tsx:47 (original from the current bitmap), StepPdf.tsx (no use of api.stale).
findings.proposal: Give each image an identity: in setPhoto set rec.imageRev = uid(), or store a SHA-256 of the blob via crypto.subtle.digest, and add it to computeKey. When replacing the photo with an existing compute, ask whether to keep the face/detail regions. In StepPdf (and the CSV export), show the stale Badge and require an explicit 'Trotzdem mit alter Berechnung exportieren' confirmation. Use the image the mosaic was computed from for 'Originalfoto': save a JPEG of it at compute time, e.g. in rec.meta or a separate store.

findings.title: Full-resolution photos are kept decoded and never released (ImageBitmap.close() is never called), and PDF object URLs leak
findings.problem: Each Workspace mount decodes the original photo at full resolution (a 48 MP phone photo is about 190 MB of RGBA). Home.newProject decodes it once more only to read the aspect ratio. Nothing calls bitmap.close(): not on photo replacement, not on unmount, not in Home. Memory stays high after leaving the project, which risks renderer or WebView crashes on Android phones (which in turn hit the unsaved-debounce problem). StepPdf also creates an object URL for every generated PDF and never revokes it, so each regeneration keeps the previous multi-MB blob alive.
findings.evidence: Measurement: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t13_bitmap_memory.cjs with big48mp.jpg (8000×6000), output t13_output.txt: Chromium RSS 'baseline 450' → 'after opening 779' → 880–1127 MB while reopening 6 times → 'after leaving project, 5 s idle 1108' MB (not released). Code: grep finds no '.close()' in src; imagePrep.ts:10-16 (full-res createImageBitmap), Home.tsx:29 and 44, useProject.ts:79/188-192, StepPdf.tsx:71 (createObjectURL with no revoke; downloadBlob in components.tsx:162-169 does revoke).
findings.proposal: On import, downscale to a working copy (long edge ≤ 4096 px, enough for 40M positions) using createImageBitmap(blob, {resizeWidth, resizeQuality:'high'}). Store it as the 'working' image and keep the original blob only for export. Call bmp.close() in Home after reading width/height, in setPhoto before replacing, and in a useProject unmount cleanup. In StepPdf, revoke the previous result.url before setResult and in a useEffect cleanup.

Low priority (impact about 2, effort S). Change only where memory is freed; image quality stays the same.

1. Keep two images in useProject.ts:
   - A preview bitmap for the screens, decoded with createImageBitmap(blob, {imageOrientation:'from-image', resizeWidth/resizeHeight so the long edge is at most 4096, resizeQuality:'high'}). StepPhoto, CropEditor, StepShapes, StepGeometry and originalPreview use it, and crop coordinates stay normalized.
   - The real photo size, kept in state as `sourceSize`. Use it for the "W x H px" label in StepPhoto.tsx:104 and for the aspect-ratio math.
2. Decode the full-resolution photo only during compute. In runCompute (useProject.ts:277-290), decode image.original, pass it to renderCropped, then call close() in a finally block right after canvasToRaw. Compute input is then exactly what it is today.
3. Call close() on the old bitmap in three places: in setPhoto before setBitmap, in a useEffect cleanup keyed on the bitmap, and in the load effect when `alive` is false.
4. In Home.tsx:29 and 44, call close() right after reading width and height.
5. In StepPdf, keep the URL in a ref. Revoke the previous URL before setResult({url}), and revoke the current one in an unmount cleanup.

Check the result with mem3.cjs: at most one bitmap alive at any time, and renderer memory down when a project is reopened.

Part A (effort S, do it now; compute results stay identical):
1. **Home.tsx:29-30 and 44-45:** close the bitmap right after reading the aspect:
   `const b = await loadBitmap(photo); aspect = b.width / b.height; b.close();`
2. **useProject.ts:79-80:** `if (alive) setBitmap(bmp); else bmp.close();`

   ```
   const liveBmp = useRef<ImageBitmap|null>(null);
   useEffect(() => { const old = liveBmp.current; liveBmp.current = bitmap; if (old && old !== bitmap) old.close(); }, [bitmap]);
   useEffect(() => () => { liveBmp.current?.close(); liveBmp.current = null; }, []);
   ```
   This is safe under StrictMode because the bitmap is still null when StrictMode does its test unmount.
4. **StepPdf `generate`:** call `api.originalPreview(1800)` and encode it before the first await, or wrap it in try/catch. Then leaving mid-generation can never draw a closed bitmap.
5. **StepPdf object URL:**
   - Create it only when `!isNative()`.
   - Keep it in `urlRef`, and revoke the previous one when a new generation starts.
   - Add `useEffect(() => () => { if (urlRef.current) URL.revokeObjectURL(urlRef.current); }, [])` above the early `if (!c || !G) return`.
6. **Regression check:** add a Playwright case that opens a project with a large photo, goes to Projects, reopens it, and checks that the photo step still shows the real pixel size and that Compute and PDF work.

Part B (effort M, optional; keep two versions of the image instead of shrinking the one used for the calculation):
1. On load, decode a preview bitmap with `createImageBitmap(blob, {imageOrientation:'from-image', resizeWidth, resizeHeight, resizeQuality:'high'})`, long edge at most 3072-4096.
2. Use it for StepPhoto, CropEditor, StepShapes and originalPreview, and for `effectiveCrop`. The crop is stored as fractions of the image, so it is the same at any size.

4. In `compute()`, decode the full-resolution original from `api.image.original` on demand, then run `renderCropped` and `canvasToRaw`, then close it right away. The working image stays exactly as today (up to 6 MP of the crop), so tight crops such as faces keep full colour detail.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
